maria: FYI nightly perf: short seq (8 tokens) tail latency up ~5-8ms on trt-vllm wrapper after the wrapper refactor.
kevin: ah ok. is that for dedicated only or hosted too?
maria: both; more visible on 1-2 GPU pods. p50 same, p95/p99 shifted.
kevin: can you paste the nsys snapshot or the quick flame? :eyes:
maria: pasted quick nsys extract below — capture started around invoke for a 8-token completion

```
NSYS_SUMMARY:
CPU: wrapper::invoke (host)  6.3ms
  -> cudaMemcpyAsync (host->device)  1.1ms
  -> trt_runner::enqueue_kernel (device) 0.9ms
  -> cudaStreamSynchronize (host)  3.8ms
  -> kv_prefetch async fire 0.2ms
GPU: big_matmul_kernel 1.2ms
     small_attention_kernel 0.6ms
     memcpy D2H 0.4ms
```

maria: note the big cpu wait at cudaStreamSynchronize — but kernel time is tiny.
dmitri: that screams host sync after enqueue. wrapper refactor added an extra sync around KV cache warmup right?
sophia: we added a defensive sync to ensure kv prefetch completion before returning control to scheduler. might be overkill for small requests.
kevin: can you share the wrapper diff? maybe swap to event-based completion.
maria: diff snippet i tested locally:

```
- cudaStreamSynchronize(stream);
+ cudaEventRecord(event, stream);
+ while (cudaEventQuery(event) == cudaErrorNotReady) {
+   // poll but yield CPU briefly
+   std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(50));
+ }
```

maria: that dropped the host-side stall to ~1.2ms in my quick run.
sophia: nice. also check that kv prefetch runs on a low-priority stream so it doesn't preempt tiny kernels on the main stream.
dmitri: perfetto trace from kevin's run shows KV prefetch memcpy happening on default stream which ended up serializing the tiny attention kernel — small kernels queued behind big memcpy.
kevin: here's the perfetto slice I grabbed: "KV_PREFETCH D2H" overlapped with tiny kernels, stream id 7. We never set stream priorities or dedicated prefetch stream in default config.

maria: so two contributing things: (1) host sync in wrapper, (2) prefetch on default stream causing serialization.
sophia: additional note: tensorrt sometimes launches large workspace kernels that block the device; if prefetch uses same stream priority it can preempt scheduling choices. stream priorities and kernel concurrency matter.
kevin: experiments to run:
- move kv prefetch to a dedicated low-prio stream
- replace synchronous cudaStreamSynchronize with event-polling or callback
- nvtx-mark all wrapper boundaries and re-run nsys with --capture-range=nvtx

maria: cmd I ran for nsys capture:
```
nsys profile --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --output=trace_ns nsys_example_binary
```
kevin: good. also run with `--cpuctx` to see where threads are blocked.
dmitri: I'll queue A/B on staging: current vs event-based + low-prio stream. will measure p99 and tokens/sec.

maria: small gotcha: event-polling loop needs to yield or use pthread_cond to avoid busy spin on high-throughput servers.
sophia: or use cudaStreamAddCallback on our internal stream lib if available, but that's deprecated on newer cuda.

maria: last note — kernel selection heuristics: when a tiny request interleaves with a warmup that triggers a larger workspace allocation, TRT may pick a different kernel variant. so isolate prefetch/allocs off the critical path.
kevin: agreed. also add an opt-in flag in runtime to disable prefetch for <16-token requests while we iterate.

perf-bot: scheduled nsys + perfetto traces for staging at 04:00 UTC, job id rf-421.

maria: action items:
- dmitri: run A/B and post traces (assigned)
- kevin: add nvtx markers + small script to extract host wait times
- sophia: add low-prio stream + opt-in short-request skip
- i'll follow up PR for event-based sync

kevin: thanks — i'll add a small dashboard chart for host-sync-time so we don't regress silently. :thumbsup:
